messages:
maria_cs: FYI — Health+ (prospect) just locked a customer pilot that needs a 48h low‑latency demo in eu-central1 next Tue. They want guaranteed <120ms p95. Sales asked me to escalate for a temporary quota bump so their demo doesn't hit our queues.

devon_sales: +1, they close quickly if demo is smooth. Procurement will be delayed if we push them to off-hours. Any way to give them a short window of higher priority?

sre_jordan: We can look but current admission control shows sustained saturation in eu-central1 the last 36h. Giving a short priority bump without capacity change will just shift queueing to others. Here's the short metric snapshot I grabbed:

```
region: eu-central1
gpu_util: 92% (sustained)
queue_depth: 134 -> 210 over 12h
p95_latency: 180ms
preemptible_slots_free: 0
```

sre_jordan: Primary constraints: 1) limited spare GPU heads in that region, 2) a few long‑running batch jobs from an existing enterprise tenant. We can temporarily change routing, but it has tradeoffs.

infra_anya: Also noting a provisioning lag — vendor reported a firmware rollout taking nodes out of rotation for a maintenance window yesterday, so capacity hasn't fully recovered. ETA to fully healthy is ~36–48h unless we spin up cross‑region nodes.

maria_cs: If we propose cross‑region (eu-west1) to the customer, is latency still acceptable? They explicitly asked for eu-central during compliance review.

sre_jordan: eu-west1 p95 to their office IP test is ~140–160ms. Might pass, but it's borderline for <120ms ask. Alternative is to do a local run in eu-central1 but with a temporary Dedicated pool (reserved) for 48h — effectively a short reserved capacity. That costs more but guarantees isolation.

carl_sales: Can we give them a clear cost and an ask so procurement can decide? They said budget is available for urgent pilot spend.

infra_anya: Quick estimate for a 48h Dedicated burst (4xA10-style nodes): ~$8k gross (cloud + infra margin). If we do a smaller config + model quantization, could be ~$3–4k. I can put together a one‑pager.

sre_jordan: Ops mitigation options:
- temporary admission_control:priority=high for their org_id (will bump them in the queue)
- create a 24–72h Dedicated pool and pin model version
- route to eu-west1 with traffic shaping + local caching of KV to reduce tokens
- recommend model quantization + reduce batch sizes for latency

maria_cs: Sales prefers priority override + smaller Dedicated pool if possible. What's the risk of doing priority override alone?

sre_jordan: Risk: other customers will see higher latency; if the backlog is long it can push us into SLO alerts. We can scope a narrow time window (e.g., 09:00–17:00 CEST for two days) and enable auto‑revert.

ops-bot: Incidentbot: note added — temporary priority approach flagged for manual approval. Please run `/ops-request priority-override --org healthplus --region eu-central1 --start 2026-04-07T07:00Z --end 2026-04-09T16:59Z --reason demo` to start request.

devon_sales: I'll get customer approval on time window and budget. If they sign, can infra_anya prepare a quick quote and SRE prepare the exact `/ops-request` payload we need to run?

infra_anya: On it. I'll draft quote and config. Also will propose the hybrid option: 2-node dedicated + priority flag to reduce cost. That should keep p95 closer to target for interactive sessions.

sre_jordan: If they insist on strict <120ms for all sessions, only full 4‑node Dedicated in eu-central1 will be safe. Otherwise hybrid should work for demo traffic patterns.

maria_cs: Thanks team. I'll circle back with customer timeline by EOD and post the procurement confirmation here. tagging @devon_sales @carl_sales to follow up.

carl_sales: Thanks. If you need signoff from legal for data residency in eu-central1, ping me and I'll loop them in.

maria_cs: Will do.
